newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - Steeper yield curve likely.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - Steeper yield curve likely.

text.p: Tame inflation figures and widespread expectations that Wednesday's meeting of UK monetary authorities will leave interest rates unchanged may help steepen the UK gilt yield curve this week, anaylsts said on Monday.
They also said that domestic political uncertainty is expected to cast a shadow over the market but is unlikely to do any real damage.
A Reuter poll of 21 economists showed no one expected Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George's meeting to sanction an interest rate rise this week.
That view has only been encouraged by very subdued producer price figures released on Monday.

Producer input prices slid a surprising 3.2 percent in November, while output prices were unchanged. Economists had predicted a fall of 0.8 percent for input prices and a rise of 0.1 percent for output prices.
"UK PPIs are positive for inflation prospects and should be seen as increasing the likelihood that rates will be kept on hold," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic advisor at the Bank of America.
These factors could also help steepen the yield curve, added Kevin Adams, gilts analyst at BZW. "(The curve) has flattened too far and too fast."
Retail price data out on Thursday will also be a focal point for the market, but economists expect November figures unchanged from October - with underlying inflation steady at 3.3 percent.

Some even speculated that the drop in producer input prices might presage a dip at the retail end. "Normally it takes a bit of time for producer figures to come out in retail numbers but with the sharp fall in input prices, you have to be a bit suspicious it might feed into RPI," said Adams.
He saw little real fallout from the political divisions searing their way through the ruling Conservative party.
"It (politics) won't be supportive but it also won't be much of a negative influence. The political scene has been uncertain for a long time now," he said.

Prime Minister John Major must deal with rebel members of his Conservative Party on Europe after he lost his one-seat majority on Friday when one member said he would no longer automatically vote with the Government.

The gilt/Bund spread is expected to hug its 190-200 basis point range, said Adams, but added that the new year should see it bounce up and over 200 on the back of strong, but potentially inflationary, economic numbers.

Merrill Lynch said in a client note that yield spreads between UK five-year gilts and Bunds looked attractive. That spread has widened out sharply over the past few months, the note said -- from 60 basis points since the end of August to stand at a pick-up of 250 basis points.
